paper.title_en: Reflected constraint algebras of open Carroll--Weyl null strings
paper.abstract_en: We study whether open null strings admit the full Carroll--Weyl gauge symmetry consistently with endpoint conditions and nontrivial physical degrees of freedom. For endpoints constrained to timelike defects, natural variations imply that any nonzero Carroll flow must be tangent to the worldsheet boundary. For a fixed linear defect through the target origin, we construct a differentiable Hamiltonian system on this branch. Its complete Carroll--Weyl generator requires no additional boundary charge. Smooth reflection defines a preserved subdomain and gives a circle interpretation to selected sine and cosine modes of the constraints. Their centreless algebra extends the two-constraint open-string algebra by the local scale constraint. An endpoint obstruction shows that this reflection condition excludes some gauge orbits of the natural interval theory: we exhibit a regular four-dimensional solution with no corresponding reflected representative. Within the reflected sector, we construct a local canonical field pair and conserved target-space Lorentz charges. A separate solution family has nonzero boost charge and a nondegenerate two-dimensional symplectic pullback. The constraint algebra, the boundary choice, and the physical observables thus provide complementary information about the open theory.
